subject: Cross-cloud flat-fee rebate & reseller passback
messages:
From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@stratusq.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Packaging question: annual flat-fee across GCP + Azure and reseller passback

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo last week — StratusQ is excited about the latency improvements on our inference workloads. Procurement asked me to follow up with a concrete packaging question so we can get to a PO.

High level ask: can Redwood sell us a single annual "cross-cloud" private offer that covers GCP and Azure usage for our inference jobs (two SKUs), priced as a flat annual fee, with a 10% reseller passback to our channel partner?

Constraints from our side:
- We need predictable monthly spend and a single invoice.
- The partner needs to receive the 10% passback in the billing flow (not as a retro credit).
- We'd like to keep the list price consistent per-SKU so our internal chargeback works.

Questions:
1) Is a single private offer across clouds supported, or do you need separate private offers per cloud?
2) Will the reseller passback be handled as a marketplace commission (Cloud reseller flow) or as a separate invoiced rebate from Redwood?
3) What documentation do you need from our partner to set the passback?

I can loop in procurement if it helps. Looking to finalize terms by next week.

Best,
Alice Monroe
Head of Platform Partnerships
StratusQ

Subject: Re: Packaging question: annual flat-fee across GCP + Azure and reseller passback

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear summary. Short answers up front, details below:

- Yes, we can support a single contract and invoice for a cross-cloud commitment, but marketplace wiring varies by provider.
- Reseller passback can be implemented two ways: a marketplace-native commission (preferred for GCP/Azure via their resell flows) or a Redwood-issued invoice-level rebate if the marketplace flow doesn't support your partner.
- We'll need the partner's marketplace vendor ID and an executed reseller agreement (short form) for the commission flow.

Notes and options:
1) Private offer topology
- Option A: Two private offers (one per cloud) linked by a single Redwood PO and invoicing umbrella. Simplest operationally for marketplaces that don't support cross-cloud private offers.
- Option B: One customer-facing contract (Redwood invoice = flat annual fee) and internal split to cloud-specific private offers for fulfillment. This hides the split from you and keeps a single invoice.

2) Passback mechanics
- Marketplace commission: partner appears on the invoice as the reseller and receives commission in the cloud marketplace settlement cycle. This requires the partner to be onboarded as a reseller in the specific cloud account.
- Redwood invoice rebate: Redwood issues the 10% rebate on our invoice to the partner. Pros: works for partners not enrolled in marketplace programs. Cons: introduces reconciliation work and delayed cash flow to partner.

3) Recommended approach
- Run Option B with marketplace commission for the cloud where the partner is already onboarded (e.g., Azure). For the other cloud (if partner not onboarded) we use the Redwood invoice rebate. This hybrid minimizes reconciliation and keeps your single invoice.

Next steps I need from you:
- Confirm which partner you want on-file for passback and provide their marketplace vendor ID(s).
- I'll attach a pricing workbook with two illustrative waterfalls (flat-fee vs SKU-anchored) and a draft partner rebate term sheet.

Attaching: pricing_workbook_v3.xlsx, partner_rebate_terms_Q2.pdf

If that sounds OK I'll loop Ben to finalize reseller margin math and produce a sample PO and DocuSign package.

Thanks,
Olga
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Packaging question: annual flat-fee across GCP + Azure and reseller passback

Looping in here with margin/ops detail.

Olga — thanks for the proposed hybrid. Quick math below for the sample workbook attached:

Scenario: flat annual fee = $600k (shops 12 months) covering two SKUs (GCP-inference, Azure-inference). StratusQ wants 10% partner passback.

- Marketplaces (if partner onboarded) pay commission on listed marketplace revenue. Typical pass-through rate is handled in marketplace settlement; Redwood's billable-to-customer number stays the same.
- If we issue a Redwood rebate instead: Redwood invoices $600k, pays partner $60k via monthly or quarterly rebate. That $60k will be recognized as contra-revenue and needs approval from finance (ops 48-72 hrs for workback).

Operational asks from finance/ops: 
- Partner banking details and tax W-8/W-9 as applicable.
- Confirmation whether partner needs monthly or quarterly payments for cashflow.
- Any SOC2/entitlement restrictions for partner access to telemetry (if passback reconciliation requires usage reports).

Suggested margins and language for contract appendix (short form):
- Passback: 10% of invoiced Redwood revenue for covered SKUs, payable quarterly within 45 days of Redwood invoice reconciliation.
- Reconciliation: Redwood will provide a monthly usage CSV to partner; disputes must be raised within 30 days.

If Alice confirms vendor IDs I will create two sample settlement flows (marketplace-settled commission + Redwood rebate) in the pricing_workbook that show net to partner, Redwood net revenue, and expected cash timing.

Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
